_readme: Window openings of the Maiden Tower. Edit this file directly — Vite hot-reloads it,
no rebuild needed. Every number here is an ESTIMATE from photographs, not a survey.
WHAT CHANGED ON 2026-08-10, AND WHY IT OUTRANKS EVERYTHING BELOW
The owner, who is Azerbaijani and has walked the building, stated, in capitals:
«НА ЯРУСАХ ОКНА ТОЛЬКО В НАЧАЛЕ И В КОНЦЕ ПРОХОДОВ ЛЕСТНИЦ.
НА САМИХ ЯРУСАХ НИКАКИХ ОКОН НЕТ»
— on the storeys, openings are ONLY at the beginning and the end of the stair
passages; on the storeys themselves there are no windows at all.
and, asked again the same day, said it a second time with more in it:
«на ярусах самих окон нет. только когда заходишь в проем чтобы подняться в
некоторых местах и вначале входа на лестницу и в конце есть окна а в
некоторых местах или в начале или в конце входа на лестиницу»
— on the storeys themselves there are no windows. Only once you step into the
passage to climb: in SOME places there is one at the beginning of the stair
entrance AND one at the end; in other places only at the beginning, or only
at the end.
[OWNER] > [PHOTO], and not as a matter of rank alone. The photographs are exterior
frames. They can see that a slit exists, how tall it is and roughly where on the drum
it sits; they cannot see which side of a four-metre wall its inner mouth opens onto.
That is precisely the question the owner answered, and it is the one thing this whole
file was silently assuming an answer to.
SO AN OPENING NO LONGER CARRIES ITS OWN AZIMUTH OR ITS OWN HEIGHT. Both are now
properties of the stair: a slit is at the end of a passage, so it is wherever that end
is. What remains editable here is what the stair cannot say — how big the hole is, how
its head is finished, and which ends are open. The photographic readings are not
deleted: they move to `photographicLadder` below, where they are the yardstick the
derived layout is SCORED against instead of the input that places it.
AND WHICH ENDS ARE OPEN IS DATA, NOT A RULE. Read this before touching
`open` on any of the twelve.
The second statement is the one that forced this. «в некоторых местах … и в начале и
в конце … а в некоторых местах или в начале или в конце» — some passages have an
opening at both ends, others at one end only. That is not a pattern; it is a list of
twelve facts, and the only person who has walked past all twelve is the owner.
The model DERIVES it in the meantime: an end is open unless the buttress or the parapet
stands in the way. That is a rule standing in for a fact, and it is published as such.
RE-DERIVED 2026-08-13, AFTER THE STAIR TURNED A QUARTER OF THE DRUM.
Every figure below is measured on the built model, end by end.
[OWNER] 2026-08-13, asked where the entrance to the stair stands when you look down on
the tower: to the RIGHT of the beak, clockwise, about a quarter of the circumference.
BUTTRESS.azimuthDeg is 106.7 [OSM], so STAIR.startAzimuthDeg is now 106.7 + 90 = 196.7
— see the long note at that constant, including why this is not the old 200 restored.
climb   end        azimuth   stone on the bearing        verdict
2→3     beginning    206.9   0 m — clear of the pier     OPEN
2→3     end          102.4   9.88 m of solid buttress    blind
3→4     beginning    206.6   0 m                         OPEN

WHAT CHANGED, AND IT IS NOT SMALL. Before the turn, five of the six FEET were dropped
as blind: they stood at azimuth 108.7–110.2 and faced 10.21–10.55 m of buttress pier.
All six are clear now. Two heads take their place, both on the low climbs. Nine ends
are cut where six were — and [OWNER] separately says the tower has TOO FEW openings,
which this was checked against rather than assumed: nine against the eight the
photographs count is the first time the derived set has OVERSHOT the photographed one.
AND THE SHAPE OF HIS OTHER SENTENCE COMES TRUE, which has to be reported carefully.
Three passages now carry an opening at both ends and three at one end only, which is
«в некоторых местах и в начале и в конце … а в некоторых местах или в начале или в
конце». Until 2026-08-13 the model had no example of the first case AND no answer he
could give would have produced one. This is CORROBORATION AND NOT A RESULT: the angle
came from his answer about the beak, the openings fell where they fell, and had they
fallen the other way this file would be recording the contradiction again. It must
never be tuned to keep this true — that is CLAUDE.md rule 7 exactly, and the reason
the old note here forbade the four degrees of turn that would have done the same job.
ONE END IS ON A KNIFE EDGE AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED AS THOUGH IT WERE FOUND. The pier's
daylight edge is at azimuth 113.5 [OSM]; head-6-7 comes out at 113.63. It is open by
0.13° — 14 mm on the drum face — so whether that opening exists at all is decided by
the fourth significant figure of a satellite trace, not by anything about the tower.
head-7-8 at 116.0 clears by 2.5°, which is better only in degree. Pinned in
passageOpenings.test.ts so a correction to the buttress cannot move it in silence.
ONE THING GOT SIMPLER FOR FREE. The buttress's head height is unresolved (level with
the parapet, against 18.3 ± 0.5 m), and until now that silhouette DECIDED how many
openings the tower had — at the low reading two feet rose clear of the pier and the
count went six to eight. It decides nothing now: the only two ends still inside the
pier stand at y 8.31 and 11.59, far below either reading, so both give the same nine.
SO `open` IS THE DATUM AND THE DAYLIGHT CHECK IS ONLY A CHECK.
open: null    [PLACEHOLDER] — nobody has been asked about this end. All twelve
ship this way. The check stands in so the model has something to
draw, `decidedBy` reads 'placeholder', and the conflict report keeps
saying the record is empty. It is NOT a shorthand for 'no'.
open: true    cut it — if the check finds daylight. Where it does not, nothing is
cut and a conflict is raised: an opening into ten metres of pier
lights nothing, and cutting one quietly would be worse than dropping
one quietly. Neither happens quietly.
open: false   shut, on the record's authority. The check is not consulted.
`openSaidBy` must be filled in whenever `open` is. An end opened or shut by nobody is
how a guess becomes a fact three commits later; validateEndRecord() refuses it.
WHAT TO ASK HIM: see `openEndsQuestion` below. Six questions, one per passage, each
answer setting two of the twelve.
THE PATTERN AGREES AND THE COUNT DOES NOT. Say both.
AGREES: this file's strongest structural reading is that the eight slits stand in
TWO COLUMNS of four. Stacked flights — rebuilt as six discrete flights one above
another at the owner's instruction — put all six feet at one bearing and all six
heads at another. Two columns, by construction, not by tuning. The upper column's
measured ~11 deg drift also acquires a mechanism for the first time: the wall thins
with height, midRadius grows from 4.20 to 5.22, stepAngle = going / midRadius falls,
so a flight of the same rise higher up sweeps less arc (88.5 deg at the bottom,
75.7 deg at the top) and each head arrives a few degrees earlier than the last.
Derived heads: 5.7 / 8.8 / 16.9 / 19.3 / 21.6, a drift of +15.9 deg over the set.
DOES NOT AGREE, three ways, all measured on the current model [re-measured 2026-08-13]:
COUNT.       Twelve flight ends. With the record empty and the check standing in,
all six feet carry a slit and three heads do; the other three are
withheld as blind. Nine openings against eight photographed slits.
The residual has changed SIGN — it was six against eight — and one
derived opening has no photographed counterpart rather than two
photographed slits having no carrier. Neither gap is filled by
invention. This count is a property of the FALLBACK, not of the
building, and it moves the day the owner answers `openEndsQuestion`.
SEPARATION.  The two derived columns stand about 97 deg apart (feet 205.4–218.5,
heads 113.6–116.0, ignoring the double-height 4→6 whose head swings
to 46.8). The photographs give 35 ± 6. UNCHANGED by the turn, and it
could not have changed: the separation is a flight's own sweep,
sweep = (rise / riser) × (going / midRadius), which rotating the
whole stack does not touch. Getting 35 deg out of one storey height
needs a going of about 0.12 m. That is not a step. Either the 35 is
wrong or the stacked-flight layout is.
RUNG PITCH.  The photographed ladder steps 0.0943 H = 2.78 m between slits; the
derived one now steps 2.46 m. THE RESIDUAL SHRANK AND FLIPPED SIGN,
from +0.50 to −0.32, and that is NOT a floor table getting better.
rungSpacing is the mean gap over whatever set is cut, so it fell
purely because three flights gained a second opening. Nothing about
the storey heights has been touched, and the conflict recorded for
upper-4 (0.94 H lands inside the derived parapet) is untouched with
it.
The 35 deg is the weakest of the three and it is worth saying where it is weak. It
was obtained by linearising pixels to degrees ('3 deg of azimuth would give 23 px')
on a drum, where x = R·sin(az − az_camera): near the limb a large azimuth difference
compresses to almost nothing, so a centre-of-frame scale UNDERSTATES the true
separation, and the camera bearing itself was recovered from the buttress silhouette
to about ±20 deg. Re-measuring one frame with an explicit camera bearing and a sine
rather than a constant px/deg is the cheapest test in this list.
A PREDICTION worth photographing, and it is SHARPER since 2026-08-13: at three
landing levels the model now cuts TWO slits about 90 deg apart — at y 21.44 the head
of 6→7 at azimuth 113.6 and the foot of 7→8 at 205.4, and the same at y 18.16 and
24.72. None of the eleven frames shows such a pair, but all eleven look at the same
side of the drum. One frame from a bearing near 200 deg settles it, and that bearing
is now where SIX of the nine derived openings are — the whole foot column. It is the
single cheapest observation anyone could bring back to this model.
A COINCIDENCE THAT USED TO BE HERE AND IS NOW WITHDRAWN: the buttress's head height
is unresolved in config/tower.ts (level with the parapet, against 18.3 ± 0.5 m), and
at the low reading two feet used to rise clear of the pier, taking the count from six
to eight — the photographed number exactly. This file warned at length that it was
not evidence for the low buttress. It is not evidence for anything now: the two ends
still inside the pier stand at y 8.31 and 11.59, below either reading, so the
silhouette no longer changes the count at all. Recorded because a warning that stops
applying should be retired out loud rather than deleted.
THERE IS NO LONGER AN OPENING IN ANY CHAMBER WALL. `chamberOpenings` is empty, and the
record of the one that used to be there is kept in `chamberOpeningsHistory` below.
WHAT WAS BELIEVED BEFORE 2026-08-10 — kept verbatim, as the record of how
the old layout was established and why it was believed
PROVENANCE. The layout comes from reading the high-resolution exterior photographs in
reference-photos/exterior/ and cross-checking eleven of them. What that established:
- 8 narrow slits, arranged in TWO columns of four, plus one arched window.
- The LOWER column (heightFraction 0.28-0.61) holds a constant azimuth: it is a true
vertical generator, confirmed to about a degree in several frames.
- The UPPER column (0.67-0.94) DRIFTS about 11 deg toward the buttress as it descends.
The drift is real: it runs opposite in sign to the perspective foreshortening of the
drum's own silhouette, and is several times larger.
- Storeys 1 and 2 carry no exterior opening at all on the photographed arc. That was
verified positively (blank masonry down to the plinth), not merely unobserved.
- The arched window is a LATER INSERTION: dressed ashlar cut through banded rubble,
modern frame. Kept here so the model matches the post-2013 building, flagged so it
can be excluded from any argument about the original design.
THE TWO COLUMNS ARE ABOUT 35 DEG APART, and they were not. Until 2026-08-09 the lower
column sat at azimuth 141 and the upper at 132-143, i.e. threaded through the middle of
each other, which put all eight slits in one vertical ladder on the drum. Re-reading the
exterior set says otherwise: on Baku Maiden Tower 004 7736.jpg the slit centres detect at
x = 971/1000/1079/1131 for the upper group and x = 701/689/681/689 for the lower, a gap of
about 360 px where 3 deg of azimuth would give 23. Four blind readings put the separation
at 38-40, 33-36 and 29-47 deg; taken together, 35 +/- 6. The lower column is therefore now
at 170 [ESTIMATE], the midpoint of the 167-174 the readings support. NOTHING ELSE MOVED:
the absolute bearing of the whole set is still the buttress, so only the RELATIVE placement
of the lower column has changed, and 170 is a judgement inside a 6 deg spread, not a
measurement. Retune it in leva against that photograph before trusting it.
[2026-08-10] The PATTERN this paragraph found was right and the CAUSE it assigned was
not. Two columns is what stacked flights produce for free; it was fitted to the frames
as a free relative placement. And the 35 deg is quantitatively incompatible with a
flight of stairs at STAIR.goingTarget — see the separation residual above.
AZIMUTHS carry roughly +/-20 deg of systematic error. They are pinned to the buttress
(106.7 deg, measured from the OSM footprint), and the bearing of each camera had to be
recovered from the buttress silhouette. Relative order and spacing are far more reliable
than the absolute values. Retune in leva against the photographs.
[2026-08-10] There is no longer a leva control for a window bearing, and there should
not be: an opening at the end of a passage has no bearing of its own. The control that
moves the slits is Staircase → start az°, and it moves all of them at once. That is
also why it must not be used to settle which ends are open — see the section above.
WHERE THE BARRIER HANGS differs by type of opening, and one rule for both is wrong
on one of them. In a slit's embrasure the wrought gate stands at the TOP of the steps,
at the outer end, just short of the slit itself — the whole flight lies between the room
and the gate. In the later arched window the grille is at the ROOM face, with a lock plate
and a keeper on the right jamb, and a glazed casement behind it. So `barrierAt` is per
opening; 'outer' is the default and only arched-later said otherwise. Two of the four blind
readings put the slit gate at the inner end, and the re-check found both wrong — worth
recording, because it means the model's original outer placement was righter than the
readings that criticised it.
[2026-08-10] The field survives and its second value is renamed 'room' → 'revealEnd',
because 'room' is now false for every slit: the far end of a slit's reveal is the stair
landing, not a chamber. The gate at the outer end of the reveal with a passage behind it
may well be the right reading of the same frame — but it is a different sentence, and
re-using the old wording would have hidden that the premise moved. With arched-later
withdrawn, 'revealEnd' is now carried by no opening at all; it is kept because the
reading it records is a reading of a photograph, and photographs do not stop being
evidence when a model changes.
HEADS. Not all flat, which is how they were modelled until 2026-08-09. Reading one frame
with one light and one camera (exterior/Qız qalası yaxından.jpg): the two topmost slits
have flat heads with a separate lintel stone over them, the ones below have clean
semicircular heads cut straight through the courses rather than built up out of voussoirs,
and the later window is a true two-centred pointed arch with a dressed voussoir surround.
Two blind readings disagreed about where flat stops — 'all round except the topmost'
against 'the top two flat, round below' — and a montage of that one frame supports the
second, which is what is recorded here. upper-2 sits on the boundary and is the value to
question first. [PHOTO], and only from one frame.
[2026-08-10] Carried across as 'the two topmost openings are flat', applied to the two
highest ends that are actually built. That is [PHOTO] for the observation and
[ASSUMPTION] for the transfer: the photographed set and the derived set are not the
same set, and no id-level correspondence between them can be established. The 'pointed'
head goes out of the shipped model with arched-later; the shape itself is still built
and tested in windowProfile(), because it is what the photographs show over that window
and the reading does not depend on whether the model cuts it.
OUTER SIZES: the 1:4.8 height-to-width ratio was measured off a slit at 5x zoom and is
solid, because both dimensions come from the same place in the frame so the scale cancels.
The absolute width is calibrated against the documented 16.5 m diameter and is good to
maybe 40 percent. INNER sizes are NOT measured at all: only one interior photograph of a
slit exists, and it gives proportion, not metres. They are modelled as a splay.
[2026-08-10] Because the inner sizes were never measured, they are now UPPER BOUNDS
rather than sizes: the passage clamps them. A 1.5 m mouth on a 4.7 m cheek spans 18.3
deg and the landing it opens off is 20.4 deg long, so the width is trimmed to keep the
mouth off the passage's end cap; the 2.4 m inner height does not fit under a 2.30 m
vault at any sill and is trimmed to about 2.0. Both clamps bite only on numbers this
file already declares unmeasured. The outer 0.4 × 1.9 is untouched.
solsticeAligned is FALSE on every opening, deliberately. No source identifies which
aperture Islamov's winter-solstice claim refers to. Setting the flag on whichever slit
happens to sit near the solstice sunrise bearing (~120.7 deg here) would decide Phase 8's
result in advance, which CLAUDE.md rule 7 forbids. Phase 8 should instead ask the open
question: which openings, if any, does the ray actually enter?
[2026-08-10] Phase 8's answer will now be a different answer. The reveal is 2.5–3.5 m
deep instead of ~4.6, so the acceptance cone is wider, and the bearings have moved by
more than 100 deg. Recompute and publish; do not adjust. Note that the nearest opening
to the solstice bearing is now the foot of the roof climb at 121.8 — an end whose
openness is a [PLACEHOLDER] standing on a fallback. Phase 8's answer is therefore
contingent on an unanswered question, and the hypotheses layer says so.

note: WHAT A READER MUST ASK THE OWNER TO FILL IN `open` ON THE TWELVE ENDS BELOW.
Do not ask about ids. `foot-4-6` is a name this repository invented; he has climbed a
stair. Ask about the climb, one flight at a time, and each answer sets two ends.
Ask it in Russian, which is the language both statements came in. Verbatim:
«Пройди мысленно каждый марш снизу вверх. Для каждого скажи: окно есть
ТОЛЬКО в начале подъёма, ТОЛЬКО в конце, И ТАМ И ТАМ, или НИ ТАМ НИ ТАМ?»
— Walk each flight in your head from the bottom up. For each one say: is there a
window ONLY at the beginning of the climb, ONLY at the end, at BOTH, or at NEITHER?
'Beginning' is the landing you step onto from the room below, before the first tread.
'End' is the landing at the top, before the doorway into the room above. Those are the
two places his own sentence names, and they are the `foot` and the `head` of a flight.
Six answers, twelve ends. `neither` is offered as a fourth option because he did not
name it and it must not be smuggled in as the default — but it is what the model
currently produces for no passage at all, so if he never uses it, nothing is lost.
[2026-08-13] THE SEVENTH QUESTION IS HALF ANSWERED. It used to read: standing in a
chamber facing the entrance, is the doorway onto the stair to your left or to your
right? He was asked the same thing from above instead — where is the entrance to the
stair relative to the beak, looking down — and said: to the RIGHT of it, clockwise,
about a quarter of the circumference. STAIR.startAzimuthDeg is derived from that now
(BUTTRESS.azimuthDeg + 90 = 196.7) and the table above is re-measured on it.
STAIR.winding is still unanswered and still moves every one of these ends: flipping
it mirrors the whole stack onto the other side of the drum. Its question is unchanged
— «поднимаясь по лестнице в стене, ось башни у тебя слева или справа?»
AND THE OLD SEVENTH IS NOW A PREDICTION RATHER THAN A QUESTION, which makes it a
cheap independent check: with the entrance at 270 and the foot doorways at about 191,
a person standing in a chamber facing the entrance has the way onto the stair some
79 deg round to their LEFT, just behind the shoulder. If he says right, the quarter
turn is wrong and everything above moves again.

passages.climb: storey 4 → storey 6 (the long flight, past storey 5)

note: WHAT SHAPE THE TOP OF AN OPENING IS. [OWNER] 2026-08-13 said only that the model has
it WRONG — «форма верха окон неправильная» — and did not say what the right shape is.
Nothing has been changed on the strength of that. The values stay where they are,
tagged, until he answers.
WHAT THE MODEL CURRENTLY BUILDS, and where it came from: round (semicircular) heads
on every opening except the three topmost, which are flat with a lintel stone over
them. That is [PHOTO] and it is ONE FRAME — exterior/«Qız qalası yaxından.jpg» — read
once, with two blind readings disagreeing about where flat stops. It was then
transferred onto the derived set by height alone, which is [ASSUMPTION]: the
photographed openings and the derived ones are not the same set and no opening-level
correspondence between them can be established.
ASK IT BY THE CLIMB, NOT BY AN ID. `head-4-6` is a name this repository invented.
Ask in Russian, verbatim:
«Пройди каждый марш снизу вверх. У окна в этом проходе верх какой:
КРУГЛЫЙ (полукругом), ПРЯМОЙ (перемычка плитой), или ОСТРЫЙ (стрельчатый)?»
— for each climb: is the top of the opening ROUND, FLAT, or POINTED?
One word per climb. If the two ends of one climb differ, say so and the field becomes
per end; today it already is per end in `passageOpenings` below, and only the answer
would be per climb.
WHAT AN ANSWER CHANGES. `head` on each of the twelve entries, which windowProfile()
turns into the cutter's outline. All three shapes are already built and tested there,
including 'pointed', which no shipped opening uses since the arched window was
withdrawn — so an answer of «острый» costs no new geometry, only a value. It changes
nothing else: not the size, not the bearing, not the sill.
IF HE MEANS SOMETHING NOT IN THAT LIST — a flat head with a relieving arch over it, a
corbelled head, a head cut on the slope of the passage vault — then it is new geometry
and none of it is in docs/. Write down what he says and stop there (rule 1).
ask: ФОРМА ВЕРХА ОКОН — [OWNER] 2026-08-13 сказал, что она неправильная, но не сказал, какая
правильная. Сейчас в модели: круглый верх везде, кроме трёх самых верхних — там прямой.
Это [PHOTO] с ОДНОГО кадра, перенесённое на другой набор проёмов по высоте [ASSUMPTION].
«Пройди каждый марш снизу вверх. У окна в этом проходе верх какой:
Одно слово на марш: 2→3, 3→4, 4→6, 6→7, 7→8, 8→крыша. Ответ меняет только поле `head`
в src/data/windows.json — все три формы уже построены в windowProfile().
Подробности и что делать с четвёртым ответом: windows.json → headShapeQuestion.note

climbs.climb: storey 4 → storey 6 (the long flight, past storey 5)

climbs.current: round at the beginning, flat at the end

note: HOW HIGH THE SILL STANDS ABOVE THE LANDING. [OWNER] 2026-08-13 said the model has it
WRONG — «высота подоконника над площадкой неправильная» — and did not say what the
right height is. Nothing has been changed on the strength of that.
WHAT THE MODEL CURRENTLY BUILDS: PASSAGE_OPENING.sillAboveLanding = 0.30 m, one
course of stone, the same thickness as a floor slab. It is a [PLACEHOLDER] and it is
not a reading of anything — it is a CONSTRUCTIONAL RULE chosen because it introduces
no new number. No source gives this dimension. The photographs cannot: re-referring
the eight measured slit centres to the nearest landing below them implies sills from
−0.43 to +2.08 m, and the median of a 2.5 m spread is a guess wearing a reading's
clothes.
IT IS BOUNDED ABOVE BY GEOMETRY, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MAKES THE ANSWER USEFUL. The
clear light over a landing is PLAYER.stairHeadroom = 2.30 m and the opening is 1.90 m
tall, so a sill anywhere in 0…0.40 m fits under the vault and anything higher does
not. 0.30 sits inside that band, which is luck rather than corroboration.
ASK IT BY THE CLIMB. In Russian, verbatim:
«Встань на площадку в конце прохода, у самого окна. Низ окна (подоконник)
у тебя на какой высоте: У ПОЛА, ПО КОЛЕНО, ПО ПОЯС или ПО ГРУДЬ?»
— standing on the landing at the opening: is the bottom of the opening at the
FLOOR, at the KNEE, at the WAIST, or at the CHEST?
One word per climb. His stature is 1.85 m [OWNER], which is already in the config for
the roof measurement, so the four answers read as roughly: floor ≈ 0, knee ≈ 0.50,
waist ≈ 1.05, chest ≈ 1.35 m.
WHAT AN ANSWER CHANGES, AND WHY IT IS BIGGER THAN IT LOOKS. «У пола» is buildable at
once. ANY OF THE OTHER THREE BREAKS THE 0.40 m BOUND ABOVE — a sill at the knee puts
the head of a 1.9 m opening 0.10 m above the passage vault — so an answer of knee,
waist or chest is not a new value for one constant. It says that at least one of
these is wrong: the 1.90 m opening height [PHOTO, ±40 percent on the absolute scale],
the 2.30 m headroom [ASSUMPTION], or the premise that the whole opening is cut in the
landing's own wall rather than climbing with the passage. Record which one he moves
and do not pick for him.
THE THIRD POSSIBILITY IS ALREADY HALF WRITTEN DOWN, in PASSAGE_OPENING.branchAtEnds:
[VIDEO] 429–449 s shows a barred branch climbing off the roof-climb landing to a slit,
and 6/3/3 steps were counted on three such branches. A sill at chest height reached by
three steps from the landing is a different building from a slit in the landing's own
wall, and it would explain a high sill without breaking anything. It is not modelled
and must not be until he says so: no source gives such a branch a length, a bearing or
a gradient.
ask: ВЫСОТА ПОДОКОННИКА НАД ПЛОЩАДКОЙ — [OWNER] 2026-08-13 сказал, что она неправильная, но
не сказал, какая правильная. Сейчас 0.30 м — [PLACEHOLDER], не измерение, а
конструктивное правило: один слой камня, толщиной с плиту пола.
«Встань на площадку в конце прохода, у самого окна. Низ окна (подоконник)
у тебя на какой высоте: У ПОЛА, ПО КОЛЕНО, ПО ПОЯС или ПО ГРУДЬ?»
ВНИМАНИЕ: свод над площадкой 2.30 м, окно 1.90 м, значит подоконник помещается только
в 0…0.40 м. «У пола» строится сразу; ЛЮБОЙ другой ответ означает, что неверно что-то
ещё — высота окна, высота свода, или само допущение, что окно вырезано в стене самой

passageOpenings.head: round
passageOpenings.note: The beginning of the climb out of storey 2, and the lowest opening in the tower. Landing centred at azimuth 206.9, 0 m of stone on the bearing — clear of the pier, whose root arc runs 72.7–113.5 [OSM] — so the fallback cuts it. IT WAS BLIND until 2026-08-13, at azimuth 110.2 facing 10.21 m of solid buttress; the quarter turn moved it. The head-on conflict this note used to record survives the move and is now sharper: it stands on STOREY 2, and the photographs record storey 2 as blank masonry down to the plinth — a POSITIVE observation, not an absence of one. [PHOTO] says there is no opening at this height on the arc it can see; the fallback cuts one at a bearing no reference frame looks at. Both can be true. If [OWNER] says this end is shut, [PHOTO] gains a corroboration and the count falls to eight.

passageOpenings.head: round
passageOpenings.note: The top of the same climb, at azimuth 102.4, facing 9.88 m of solid buttress: withheld. IT WAS OPEN until 2026-08-13, at azimuth 5.7 and clear — this is one of the two ends the quarter turn cost. If [OWNER] answers «и в начале и в конце» for this climb the model will refuse to cut it and say why, which is the right behaviour and the sharpest remaining question about the tower.

passageOpenings.head: round

The bearing is no longer a [PLACEHOLDER] — it is [OWNER] testimony resolved against the [OSM] buttress — but it is testimony about a quarter turn given by eye, so read ±15° with it.

passageOpenings.head: round

It was at 8.8 and clear before 2026-08-13, and the interior hotspot `passage-slit` stood on this landing; the marker was moved when the end went dark, and it is derived from the built set now rather than named, because a marker on blank masonry renders exactly like a marker on a hole. passageOpenings.head: round

passageOpenings.head: round
passageOpenings.note: Azimuth 113.63 against a pier whose daylight edge is at 113.5 [OSM]. OPEN BY 0.13 DEGREES — 14 mm on the drum face — and that is the whole of the evidence for it. Whether this opening exists is decided by the fourth significant figure of a satellite trace, not by anything about the tower: one step of the leva slider deletes it, and a survey correcting the buttress bearing by a quarter of a degree either way settles it in one direction or the other. Pinned in passageOpenings.test.ts so it cannot move in silence. passageOpenings.head: flat
passageOpenings.note: Azimuth 218.5, 0 m of stone on the bearing: cut. The roof climb's interior landing is paid for in arc, so its flight starts 13 deg further round than the others and this end sits apart from the other five feet. It stands at the same height as head-7-8, about 103 deg away — the pair no photograph has yet shown. TWO THINGS COME CLOSEST TO IT AND NEITHER TOUCHES: the downpipe's chase at azimuth 230, which this reveal overlaps by 0.2 deg in plan and misses by 1.98 m in height (the chase stops at the storey-7 springing), and the roof breach in the parapet, which the quarter turn moved to azimuth 110–160 and away from here. It was also, before 2026-08-13, the opening nearest the winter-solstice sunrise bearing; at 218.5 it is not, and Phase 8 must be recomputed rather than adjusted.

passageOpenings.head: flat
passageOpenings.note: The roof landing, azimuth 118.3 (was 21.6 before 2026-08-13). There is no wall above it — the deck is at 26.75 and the parapet's top at 27.5 — so a 1.9 m slit would stand 1.45 m proud of the tower. This end is already a door onto the roof. The one end whose blindness is about the BUILDING rather than about a bearing: it is unaffected by the quarter turn, and the one place `open: true` would be hardest to honour. See ROOF_QUESTION in config/tower.ts, which is the same hole in the record seen from the other side.

note: EMPTY, AND THIS IS WHY. The record is kept; the opening is not.
Until 2026-08-10 one opening stood in a chamber wall: `arched-later`, a two-centred
pointed window at azimuth 123, heightFraction 0.5 (y 12.75, storey 4), outer 0.9 × 1.6
and inner 1.8 × 2.4, grille at the room face with a lock plate and a keeper on the
right jamb and a glazed casement behind it.
WHY IT WAS BELIEVED TO BE A LATER INSERTION, and that reading is unchanged: dressed
ashlar cut through banded rubble, with a modern frame. Nothing about the photographs
has been revised. It also sat close to the drum/buttress re-entrant — 119.9–126.1 with
its ±3.1 deg outer half-width, against a root arc ending at 113.5 [OSM] — clearing the
pier by about 6 deg, which was a small independent check on the [OSM] buttress bearing
and is now a check with nothing to run on.
WHY IT WAS KEPT ON 2026-08-10, in one commit and one commit only. The owner's first
statement — no windows on the storeys — reads literally as a denial of this window too.
The argument for keeping it was that he was describing how the building WORKS, that a
later insertion is by definition outside that (somebody cut a window where they wanted
one), that its own fittings agree (lock plate, keeper and casement are chamber-face
hardware with nowhere to hang in a passage), and that CLAUDE.md's target is the tower
AS IT STANDS, modern insertions included. The window carried a `questionedBy` field
with his quote and the verbatim question to put back to him.
THE OWNER OVERRULED IT. Put the question, he did not accept the exception: he restated
the same thing — «на ярусах самих окон нет» — and went on to describe where the
openings ARE, end by end, without an exception for anything. Two statements, the second
made with the first one's counter-argument in front of him, and the counter-argument
was mine. It was a judgement about how to read testimony, and the person whose
testimony it is has now read it twice the other way.
So chamberOpenings is empty and the machinery that only ever served it is gone rather
than left idle: ChamberWindowSpec, validateChamberWindow(), windowCentreY(),
windowStoreyIndex() and sillAboveFloor() are deleted from src/lib/windows.ts, App.tsx
no longer builds a cut from this file, and the 'pointed' head leaves the shipped model
(the shape is still built and tested in windowProfile(), because it is what the
photographs show and that does not change). What stays in windows.ts is the arithmetic
that applies to the openings that DO exist: splayHalfAngleDeg, flaresInward,
solsticeWindows, groupByAzimuth.
WHAT WOULD BRING IT BACK, so that this is a decision and not an erasure: the owner
saying that the modern window on storey 4 is an exception after all, or a survey of
İçərişəhər's records showing a 21st-century intervention cut through a chamber wall.
Every number needed to restore it is in the paragraph above; nothing has to be
recovered from a diff.
ONE THING RECORDED WITHOUT BEING ASSERTED, because it did not go away with the window:
ENTRANCE in config/tower.ts concludes that [ref]'s 'south-east door' is a DIFFERENT
opening — a door to nowhere partway up the tower, and the one Islamov's winter-solstice
claim concerns. This window was at azimuth 123, halfway up, by the buttress re-entrant,
and it may have been that door. [ASSUMPTION]. If it was, the model no longer contains
it anywhere, and that is a gap to name rather than to fill.
